title: Bell and Winter
premise: August Oyelaran arrives at Hollowmere School to teach the handful of students whose classmates keep vanishing from attendance rolls without explanation. When a construction crew breaks ground for a new wing and unearths an iron door sealed from the inside, August's meticulous documentation becomes the only map of what the town has been feeding—and what it invited in generations ago. As the well beneath the school refills with each sunset, August and the remaining students, bound into an unlikely found family, must survive one night in the building while deciding whether loyalty to Hollowmere's living descendants matters more than exposing the truth that will end the disappearances forever. At dawn they open the door themselves, speak the names of the taken aloud, and let the truth drain the well dry—though August pays for it by becoming the last name on the list.
about_author: Ada Quintana is a former rural schoolteacher who spent six years collecting oral histories from towns that preferred to be forgotten. She writes horror about institutions, ledgers, and the things communities agree not to see.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: POV: August. August arrives at Hollowmere School, notices the class rosters have gaps no one will explain, and begins a private log of every oddity—the humming in the pipes, the well cap behind the gym, the way students flinch at roll call. Emotional beat: wary curiosity hardening into quiet resolve; documentation as both coping mechanism and first act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Roster That Shrinks
chapters.summary: POV: August. A student named Priya stops attending mid-week; her desk is removed overnight and her name fades from the printed roster. The principal, Mrs. Aldous, offers cheerful non-answers, but the janitor, Wren, slips August a decades-old photo showing children who match the vanished ones exactly. Emotional beat: creeping dread; the first crack in the school's polite facade.

chapters.title: Groundbreaking
chapters.summary: POV: August, shifting briefly to foreman Dez. The excavation crew strikes iron twelve feet down: a door, bolted and welded from the inside, ringed with handprints pressed into corroded metal. That night the school's lights burn blue and every clock in the building reads 3:07. Emotional beat: awe curdling into violation—the past has been disturbed and knows it.

chapters.title: Wren's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Wren shows August his predecessor's hidden ledger: every disappearance since 1911, each entry ending with the same phrase—'the well takes its share.' He confesses the staff have always known, trading silence for the school's survival. Emotional beat: betrayal and grief; loyalty revealed as complicity, and August's faith in documentation shaken by a record kept to conceal rather than reveal.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: POV: August. In the archive cellar, August finds the founding covenant: Hollowmere's first headmaster invited something up from the aquifer to end a famine, sealing the door behind it and agreeing to feed it names. The current 'missing-class problem' is the debt still being paid. Emotional beat: horrified clarity; inheritance reframed as a contract August's arrival has legally reactivated.

chapters.title: The Chosen Few
chapters.summary: POV: alternating among four remaining students—Tomas, Imani, Dev, and quiet Bethel—who have pieced together their own version of the truth. They confront August, demanding to be included rather than protected. Emotional beat: fierce solidarity; the found family forms deliberately, choosing each other over the adults' managed ignorance.

chapters.title: Sunset Clause
chapters.summary: POV: August. The door's seals begin failing as the water table rises; Mrs. Aldous attempts to sacrifice Dev to buy another generation, revealing she is the last descendant of the original signatories. August intervenes, and the group barricades itself in the library as the school starts filling with water that flows uphill. Emotional beat: terror and resolve; the night vigil begins with sunrise as the only deadline.

chapters.title: Names in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV: Bethel. Through the flooded halls, the taken appear—not monstrous but pleading, wearing the faces of a century of missing students. Bethel realizes they aren't attacking; they're asking to be remembered. The group recites names from Wren's ledger until the shapes steady and listen. Emotional beat: compassion inside horror; memory as resistance, and the discovery that the entity feeds on forgetting, not flesh.

chapters.title: The Door From Either Side
chapters.summary: POV: August. At the lowest hour, the group reaches the unearthed door. To end the covenant they must open it and speak every name—including the founder's own confession—into the dark. Mrs. Aldous makes a final stand; Wren dies holding the door's counterweight so the others can read the full ledger aloud. Emotional beat: sacrificial climax; loyalty fulfilled not through silence but through testimony.

chapters.title: First Bell
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas, then August's final log entry. Sunrise drains the well; the water recedes, the door stands open on empty stone, and the vanished names return permanently to the rosters—as memorials, not mysteries. The survivors rebuild the school around the truth instead of over it. August's last entry, written in a steadier hand than the first, closes the book. Emotional beat: mourning braided with hope; inheritance transformed into remembrance.
